name: Does Colorado's dry climate affect interior wall tile installations?

mainEntity.name: Does Colorado's dry climate affect interior wall tile installations?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, seasonal shifts between dry winters and humid summer spells cause residential framing timber to expand and contract. For wall tile, this movement can cause grout to crack or tiles to pop if joints are rigid. Professional installers handle this local climate issue by using flexible, polymer-modified thinset mortars and leaving expansion joints at floor transitions, ceilings, and inside wall corners. Filling these corner joints with flexible silicone caulk rather than rigid grout prevents cracking as your home adjusts through Colorado seasons.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Shifts in indoor humidity cause wall studs to shift, so installers use flexible modified mortars and silicone expansion joints at corners to prevent cracking.
